title: TCPL Packaging Ltd-$ - 523301 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q2 FY27 consolidated total income rose 20.2% YoY to INR 564.6 crore; EBITDA crossed INR 100 crore at 17.7% margin, PAT up 57.7% to INR 45.3 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported its first quarter with total income above INR 500 crore and EBITDA above INR 100 crore, with growth described as broad-based across domestic paperboard and flexible packaging. Management attributed growth to a mix of price and volume, with domestic volumes strong and exports described as satisfactory despite freight and geopolitical headwinds. The company incorporated TCPL Energy Materials Ltd on 24 September 2026 to pursue lithium-ion battery separator films, with a phased, calibrated plan. The Noida hard-packaging subsidiary (COPPL) lagged expectations due to weak smartphone volumes and export delays.

segments.name: Paperboard and flexible packaging (India)
segments.commentary: Domestic business sustained double-digit growth; flexible packaging (about one-quarter of the business) grew faster than paperboard, per management. Split is disclosed only annually.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Growth described as satisfactory but below hopes, particularly for the US, due to freight and logistics disruption; geographic mix broadly unchanged.

segments.name: Noida hard-packaging subsidiary (COPPL)
segments.commentary: Growth disappointing and below expectation, attributed to memory-chip price spike depressing smartphone volumes and delayed export-oriented business. Management calls it temporary.

segments.name: Creative offset
segments.commentary: Positive at EBITDA level, per management; no figures given.

segments.name: Battery separator films (TCPL Energy Materials Ltd)
segments.commentary: Wholly owned subsidiary incorporated 24 September 2026; initial phase at up to INR 200 crore investment, potentially INR 1,000-2,000 crore at full scale over a couple of years, per management.

guidance_outlook: No formal numerical guidance; management aims to sustain historical revenue growth trajectory and enhance cash generation.
Management declined to give EBITDA margin trajectory; said margins are healthy and large near-term jumps are not practical.
Separator business: phased ramp-up over five to six years; benefit to group margins described as a multi-year matter with no timeline given.
Chennai facility: utilisation steadily improving; another line hoped for sometime next year.
Debt at around 2x debt/EBITDA considered reasonable; no priority to reduce.
capex_capacity: Battery separator films: first phase uses wet-process water-based coating lines, with later backward integration into polyethylene film extrusion (larger investment).
Battery separator sizing per management: about 8-12 million square metres per GWh of cell capacity; separator cost about 6-10% of cell cost (not pack cost).
Customers named in public domain as the initial target set: Reliance, Amara Raja, Exide, Ola; export opportunities also being pursued.
Chennai facility: utilisation improving; next line possible next year.
Working capital needs for separator business described as nothing significant, number not yet given.
demand_pricing: Volume and price both contributed to Q2 growth; volume strongest in domestic and flexible packaging.
Margin improvement attributed to pricing actions, favourable mix and operating leverage, despite elevated raw material and logistics costs.
Management said demand has not been a problem in recent months; flexible packaging demand had been a concern in earlier quarters.
Smartphone-linked demand at Noida is weak; management pointing to premium cosmetics, perfumes, creams and gifting as growth areas.
Separator prices are up globally, per management; localisation by Indian cell makers cited as the route to price competitiveness against China.
Freight and logistics costs described as a major challenge, making customers reluctant to add new suppliers.

qa_highlights.question: How much of growth was price-led versus export-led, and is it sustainable into H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was a good mix of price and volume, with volume strongest in domestic and flexible packaging; performance was domestic-led and exports also grew.

qa_highlights.question: Is working capital deteriorating?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there has been no material change; working capital debt is virtually flat, and the company is not happy at current levels but percentages have not worsened.

qa_highlights.question: What is the separator plant's chemistry and process strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant is chemistry-agnostic (LFP and NMC, cylindrical, prismatic and pouch). Starts with water-based wet-process coating, then backward integration to extrusion; management said the process is similar to Sembcorp's.

qa_highlights.question: What is the moat in separators?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited process know-how, customer qualification cycles that are long despite being shorter than anode/cathode, and the absence of Indian peers today.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Noida (COPPL) growing slowly?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited memory-chip price spike depressing smartphone volumes, and export-oriented business that did not materialise due to the war and geopolitical disruption; expects a bounce back as conditions normalise.

qa_highlights.question: Separator customers and EBITDA margin for the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers are in public domain (Reliance, Amara Raja, Exide, Ola); no contracts signed yet as plant is not up. Management declined to give a sustainable EBITDA margin for the business.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a revenue CAGR target?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal guidance; the aim is to continue historical growth trajectory.

risks_watch: Separator project execution: phased ramp, unproven technology in India, and competition from China-based imports; management said pricing and localisation are key.
Export recovery: US growth slower than hoped due to freight disruption; geopolitical environment.
COPPL (Noida) volumes depend on smartphone demand recovery after memory-chip price increase.
Raw material and logistics cost inflation; management declined to give margin trajectory beyond the current quarter.
Working capital: management said it is not happy at current levels; no separator working capital figure given.
summary.management_tone: Confident on core packaging performance and reported numbers, but guarded on forward margins and separator economics, repeatedly declining to quantify margins, separator EBITDA, or customer contracts. Tone was defensive on Noida and exports, attributing shortfalls to temporary external disruption.
key_quotes: Our performance reflects sustained business momentum, healthy customer demand across our packaging segment and a continued focus on operational efficiencies, customer relationships and profitable growth.

Separator is not a natural extension of our core business, although they do utilise similar processes, and it is a very large-scale emerging opportunity, and we wanted to diversify our product portfolio.
So it is not like it is an easy process at all. It is very complex and technical.
So, to expect some big jump on it is not really practical.

adds.what: Battery separator films (TCPL Energy Materials Ltd) initial phase, wet-process water-based coating lines, up to INR 200 crore investment
Chennai facility: another line hoped for sometime next year

growth.why: Management hopes to continue its historical growth rate with no numerical guidance; Q2 total income rose 20.2% and EBITDA 27.5%, backed by volume and pricing/mix, but no specific orders or capacity numbers were given for the next four quarters beyond a separator phase up to INR 200 crore with no timeline and an unspecified Chennai line next year.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin 17.7% (c.+100 bps YoY) on pricing, mix and operating leverage, but management declined to give a margin trajectory and said large near-term jumps are not practical, while raw material and logistics costs stay elevated.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Chennai utilisation is steadily improving and another line is hoped for sometime next year, but no date or capex figure was given; separator plant (up to INR 200 crore initial phase) is approved with no commissioning timeline.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Domestic volumes were strong with double-digit growth and flexible packaging (about a quarter of business) growing faster than paperboard; H1 total income rose 18.2% YoY, though Noida and exports are soft.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is improving but not quantified, and the battery separator programme (initial phase up to INR 200 crore, full scale INR 1,000-2,000 crore over a couple of years) is already approved, so a further capex announcement depends on execution.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numerical guidance was given; management only hopes to continue its historical growth rate, so there is no formal guide to raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: COPPL Noida is running below expectation on weak smartphone volumes, exports are slower than hoped due to US freight disruption, and freight and raw material costs are elevated.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Battery separator films are in an initial wet-process phase with no commissioning date and no contracts signed yet; management is also pushing premium cosmetics and gifting packaging but gave no launch detail.

rows.label: Battery separator films via TCPL Energy Materials Ltd
rows.why: Initial phase up to INR 200 crore wet-process lines targeting Reliance, Amara Raja, Exide and Ola, with full scale INR 1,000-2,000 crore over a couple of years, but no contracts signed and no timeline for group margin benefit.

rows.label: COPPL Noida recovery
rows.why: Management calls the smartphone and export shortfall temporary and expects a bounce back, but gave no number and the memory-chip price spike is still weighing on volumes.

rows.label: Working capital not improving
rows.why: Management said it is not happy with current levels, working capital debt is virtually flat, and there is no separator working capital figure yet.

tone.note: Management was confident on core packaging growth and reported numbers, but guarded on forward margins, separator economics and customer contracts, and defensive on Noida and exports; analysts pressed on margin sustainability and the separator business.
